sounds.prompt: One loud sharp bang of a small gunpowder cap at the very start, then immediately a fast dry electric ticking crackle for one second that stops abruptly. A 1980s police stun gun firing its darts. Recorded close, dry, no reverb, no tone, no hum, no music, no voice, no laser.
sounds.reason: No take put a pop before the crackle (five takes, two prompts), so the pop is its own generation laid over the start. Take 1 is the crackle: 23 even broadband ticks in 1.04 s (about 22 per second) that end on a tick. Take 2 has swept tones and a steady 11 kHz line (reads as a synthetic zap); take 3 has the same tonal band and its one pop at the end; takes 4 and 5 are sparse single ticks (20 and 16 per second with gaps), a relay more than an arc. One take only: a weapon that sounds different on every shot reads as a different weapon.

sounds.prompt: A single sharp small bang of a toy cap gun, one shot only. Recorded close, dry, no reverb, no echo, no voice.
sounds.reason: Take 2 for the shot's first 100 ms: its peak is 7 ms in and the body is gone by about 120 ms; take 1 rings for 300 ms on a 2 kHz band.

sounds.prompt: One single dry click of a plastic trigger switch on a small handheld device, nothing else. Recorded close, dry, no reverb, no spark, no voice.
sounds.reason: All three are one click of 60 to 90 ms with nothing after it; three for variety on repeated trigger pulls.

sounds.prompt: A small hard plastic cartridge is unlatched and pulled out of a handheld device: a short latch click, then a brief plastic scrape. Recorded close, dry, no reverb, no voice.
sounds.reason: Take 3 is the prompt in order and on time: a click 19 ms in, then a light scrape. Takes 1 and 2 put their loudest click about 370 ms in, which would trail the hand in the reload animation.

sounds.prompt: A small hard plastic cartridge is pushed into a handheld device and snaps into place with one firm click. Recorded close, dry, no reverb, no voice.
sounds.reason: Take 2: a short push and a click 54 ms in. Take 3: one firm low click, 80 ms. Take 1's click comes 346 ms in, too late for the animation event.

sounds.prompt: Continuous steady electric arc crackle from a stun gun: fast ticking sparks at about fifteen pulses per second, constant level from start to end. Recorded close, dry, no reverb, no hum, no music, no voice, no science-fiction sound.
sounds.reason: Take 2 is an even train of about 40 broadband ticks in 2.2 s (18 per second) at a constant level, so the loop has no pattern to notice. Take 1 has gaps of 100 ms and more that would repeat every loop; take 3 is a steady hiss with no ticks.
